poc_plan: 4-week Dedicated POC. Week1: reserved pool provisioning + onboarding (VPC peering test, KMS key exchange). Week2: run canary (10% traffic -> dedicated) for 72h with synthetic load + production shadowing. Week3: scale to 50% traffic, run fault-injection for region failover (eu-west-1 fallback) and validate model-variant routing. Week4: rollback drills, SLA verification, cost telemetry collection and final acceptance. Acceptance criteria: p95 latency <=150ms for chat endpoints, sustained throughput 200-300 rps for batch workloads, quality delta vs hosted baseline <2% on eval prompt set, cost per 1k tokens within estimated band. Failure criteria and rollback plan documented; explicit cutoff and auto-fallback to hosted API if any node pool degradation or latency spike >30%.
notes:
CRM notes:
- Customer: Copperleaf Runtime Labs (mid-market product company building a customer support assistant + doc search and summarization flows).
- Initial ask: started on Hosted API to validate models, now evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation. Wants canary + fallback plan before committing to reserved capacity.
- From call (Alex, PM): "We need predictable latency for peak window and an easy rollback if quality or latency regressions appear."
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML integration mandatory, KMS + audit logs required for compliance. Data residency: primary in us-west, backup in eu-west.
- Infra constraints: corporate firewall requires static egress IPs for VPC peering; security team wants port/IP whitelists at least 5 business days before POC start.
- POC specifics discussed:
  * Canary traffic split: start at 10% (production routing via Redwood gateway), monitor for 48-72h.
  * Model variants: prefer gpt-like open model v1 (quantized) as primary on Dedicated; fallback to hosted tuned variant if quality drops. Also ask for an L3 variant (smaller quantized) for cost-sensitive routes.
  * Routing rules: latency-first for chat (route to nearest region/pool), cost-aware for background reranking jobs, forced region residency for certain enterprise accounts.
  * Region failover: plan to test failover from us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 using synthetic traffic; document DNS and regional routing TTLs, and SLO for RTO <= 3 mins for non-stateful requests.
  * Rollback playbook: automatic traffic reweight to hosted API on health/failure alerts, manual rollback via console with audit trail, and postmortem template (Jira ticket per incident).
- Ops & metrics: Redwood console to provide token-level cost, per-model latency breakdown, and trace links. Customer wants weekly cost forecast for committed tier.
- Commercial: requested committed throughput tiers and overage model; finance asked for a 12-month and 24-month quote. Pricing deck linked (drive://redwood/pricing/copperleaf-dedicated-sow-v2.pdf).
- Blockers: procurement wants final SOW and legal redlines; security needs completed network egress/peering checklist.
- Quote: initial ARR estimate 120k-350k depending on committed throughput and retention add-ons.
- Quote/Next steps: deliver final SOW + canary runbook by 2026-03-14, kick off Dedicated POC after PO and whitelisting.
- Quick wins: enable caching for doc-search to reduce per-token cost; suggest quantized model variants for lower-cost reranking.
- Internal notes for AE/SE: coordinate SE Diego for SLO tuning, infra runbook, and finalize KMS key handshake flow. Create INF-8921 for network setup priority.
